survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: TIMSS 1999 used a complex multistage sampling design to select nationally representative samples of eighth-grade students in participating countries. The study computed sampling weights to account for differential probabilities of student selection and to adjust for non-participation, and these sampling weights were incorporated into the international database alongside the achievement scaling results. For uncertainty estimation of reported statistics, TIMSS used jackknife replicate procedures to estimate standard errors. The technical report describes the derivation and use of sampling weights and the jackknife approach, but it does not provide a single explicit weight variable name in the excerpt; analysts should use the TIMSS-provided sampling weights and replicate weights from the international database when conducting secondary analyses.

data.outcome_summary: TIMSS 1999 is a cross-national achievement study that assessed eighth-grade students in mathematics and science across 38 participating countries, with a focus on measuring trends since the 1995 TIMSS cycle (TIMSS-Repeat). The study used a rotated test design with eight booklets and 26 item clusters, ensuring that not all students responded to all items while maintaining broad content coverage. Achievement scaling relied primarily on item response theory (IRT), producing scale scores for mathematics overall and five mathematics content areas, and for science overall and six science content areas. To quantify uncertainty in proficiency estimates, the report describes plausible-value technology generating five separate estimates per student. The technical report also documents translation and verification procedures, extensive data cleaning and quality assurance, and the use of sampling weights and jackknife replicate methods for standard errors. International benchmarks were anchored using the 90th, 75th, 50th, and 25th percentiles.
